indicators.title: Economic indicators
indicators.subtitle: Macro series the forecasting model draws on. Read only.
indicators.explainer: This index tracks what a fixed basket of everyday goods costs. When it climbs, money is losing buying power and all prices — vegetables included — drift up with it. The forecasting model reads it as background inflation, so it can tell a crop that is genuinely getting scarce apart from prices that are simply rising everywhere.
indicators.gaugeZoneNote: Headline year-on-year inflation. Zones: below 0% prices falling, 0–6% mild (around the Central Bank's target), 6–11% elevated, above 11% high.
indicators.vintageNote: Each point shows two dates: the period it describes, and when it was published. Both matter — the value only became knowable on the publish date.
indicators.revisionNote: {{count}} earlier estimate(s) were later revised. The charts show the most recently published figure for each period.
indicators.noData: No data for this series yet.

news.title: News
news.subtitle: What the news pipeline collected, and how it may move prices.
news.explainer: Articles are collected and classified automatically. The category and expected effect are simple rules of thumb (e.g. flood news usually lifts prices), not model predictions — open the article to judge for yourself.

impact.pest: Pest or disease outbreaks can damage harvests — less supply usually pushes prices up.
impact.flood: Floods can destroy crops and block transport — less supply usually pushes prices up.
impact.drought: Drought cuts yields — less supply usually pushes prices up.
impact.import_ban: Import restrictions reduce foreign supply — local prices often rise.
impact.fertiliser: Fertiliser news changes growing costs — shortages push prices up, good supply eases them.
impact.policy: Government decisions can move prices either way — open the article for the details.
impact.general: General news — no direct effect on crop prices expected.
impact.unscored: Not classified yet — this article will be scored on the next pipeline run.

news.emptyBody: The news pipeline hasn't captured any articles yet.
news.emptyFiltered: No articles match this category. Try "All news".

training.explainer: Each row is one model-training run. The gate decides whether a newly trained model is good enough to promote; the model actually serving forecasts now is marked Live. Lower MAE is better.
training.overrideNote: This model is serving now even though the gate declined it — a manual override. The decision below explains why.

userActivity.explainer: Everything the system and its users did — sign-ins, user changes, and admin edits. Failed sign-ins show the username that was tried — an unverified attempt, not a confirmed account.

errors.title: System errors
errors.explainer: Each row is one unexpected server error (a 500) that the app did not handle. The trace id matches the reference shown to the person who hit the error, so you can match a report to a row. Ordinary form and validation problems (400s) are not listed here.
errors.emptyBody: Nothing has gone wrong on the server — no unexpected errors have been recorded.

forecastAccuracy.explainer: Every night the system records the forecast it would give for each crop that day. Once that crop's harvest day passes and the market price for that day is known, the row is scored against it. Model forecasts and fallback forecasts are always counted separately.
forecastAccuracy.ledgerEmptyBody: Forecasts are recorded nightly. Accuracy appears here once harvest days start passing and their market prices are known, so expect this to stay empty for the first few months.
forecastAccuracy.countsScope: Every forecast recorded so far (all time).
forecastAccuracy.splitNote: Model forecasts and fallback forecasts are counted separately and never combined. A fallback is a crop average rather than a prediction, so a single blended number would hide which of the two you are looking at.
forecastAccuracy.noMetricsBody: No recorded forecast has reached its harvest day yet, so there is nothing to score. These figures appear as rows are scored.
forecastAccuracy.signedBiasHint: The average of forecast minus actual, in rupees per kilo. Above zero means the forecasts came in higher than the price that was actually paid.
forecastAccuracy.gapBelow: {{points}} points below — the band is too narrow
forecastAccuracy.gapAbove: {{points}} points above — the band is wider than it needs to be
forecastAccuracy.snapshotsEmptyBody: No forecast has been recorded yet.
forecastAccuracy.snapshotsEmptyBodyFiltered: No recorded forecast matches these filters. Try another version, or turn off “Scored forecasts only”.
forecastAccuracy.insideBand: The actual price fell inside the band
forecastAccuracy.outsideBand: The actual price fell outside the band

missing.title: Last night's data update did not run
missing.body: No pipeline run was recorded for {{date}}. Prices, forecasts and recommendations are still built from older data until it runs.

failed.title: Last night's data update failed
failed.body: The run for {{date}} stopped with an error, so the day's data may be incomplete or unchecked. Check the run details before trusting today's numbers.

gateBlocked.title: Last night's data update was blocked at the quality check
gateBlocked.body: The data collected for {{date}} did not pass the quality check, so it was not used. Forecasts are still built from the last data that passed.

partial.title: Last night's data update ran only partly
partial.body: Some sources did not finish for {{date}}, so part of that day's data is missing. Forecasts still work, but they may be less accurate.

ingestion.title: Ingestion runs
ingestion.subtitle: Data pipeline runs and freshness checks.
ingestion.explainer: This is where market prices, weather and economic data enter the system. Each run fetches from one source; verification checks whether the new data looks sane before the model uses it.

service.startBody: This runs one ingestion pass now on the server: each source is asked for its latest data.
service.startScope: It runs ingestion only. Verification, feature building and model training stay with the nightly pipeline — this button does not start them.
service.stopBody: This asks the server to cancel the ingestion pass that is running now.
service.stopScope: It can only cancel a pass that was started from this screen. The scheduled nightly pass runs on a separate worker and cannot be stopped here.
service.startedNotice: Ingestion pass started (batch {{batch}}). The status below refreshes as it runs.
service.stoppedNotice: Stop requested. The pass ends as soon as the server can cancel it.
service.alreadyRunning: An ingestion pass is already running, so a second one was not started. The status below has been refreshed.
service.notRunning: No ingestion pass is running, so there was nothing to stop. The status below has been refreshed.
service.notStoppable: This pass was started by the scheduled nightly job, not from this screen, so it cannot be stopped here.
service.unknownNote: The service state could not be read. Starting is still safe: the server refuses a second pass if one is already running.

ingestion.checksUnavailable: Verification details are unavailable for this run.
ingestion.emptyBody: No ingestion runs match this view yet.
